brief.recommendation: Checkout success at 55% (TEL-1) with no SLO/revenue data available (BIZ-1, BIZ-3, BIZ-5). audit.report: A batch_worker (pid 331788) in 'idle in transaction' state blocked checkout operations for 157.6 seconds, reducing checkout success to 55% (33/60 requests). The Database Guardian proposed waiting three times, citing the blocker's short 4.1s transaction with only 'SELECT 1' executed. The Continuity Guardian twice requested revision because business federation was down, making workload registry, change calendar, and tradeoff data unavailable for batch_replayable_inventory. Both guardians agreed to escalate to human on-call after three rounds when required business evidence remained inaccessible.
audit.root_cause: A transient batch_worker transaction (pid 331788) held locks while idle in transaction, blocking checkout traffic, while business federation outage prevented evidence-based risk assessment.
lessons: Pre-register batch_replayable_inventory in the workload registry with explicit replayability and interrupt policy so decisions don't stall when business federation is down.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian repeated the same wait proposal across R1-R2 without new evidence, wasting a round; the Continuity Guardian correctly held invariants but could not progress without federation data. Neither guardian could satisfy I2/I4/I7 without the missing business evidence.
follow_ups: Restore business federation connectivity and verify workload registry entries for batch_replayable_inventory.
Define and document a default interrupt policy for batch workloads when registry is unreachable.
Review batch_worker transaction patterns to prevent idle-in-transaction states during peak checkout hours.
